Jordan / team — I dug into deployment history for the FieldScale tenant. No control-plane rollout was scheduled at 08:45 PDT. However, we saw a transient increase in queued requests to the serving pool between 08:38–08:52 (spike consistent with a client-side retry storm).

I’ve asked Platform to pull the autoscaler logs; attaching our initial filter of the error rate.

Initial notes:
- No config change or model swap at that time.
- Proxy layer returned ECONNRESET for a subset of connections while the pool was scaling.
- This looks like a capacity spin / backpressure event rather than an outright outage.

Jordan — would you be able to share whether FieldScale’s integration retries are exponential backoff or immediate retries? If we can confirm a retry pattern we can propose a mitigation (rate-limiting advisories + a longer retry window).

Camila

Subject: Re: Production errors — FieldScale -> Redwood connector failures

Thanks all — ran the traces for tenant fs-2046 (matching the logs Jordan sent). Root cause summary:

- Cause: transient spike of small parallel requests from FieldScale triggered a continuous-batching pressure point in our serving runtime. During autoscaler scale-up there was a short window (~45s) where connection queueing and proxy resets occurred.
- Impact: ~11–14% requests returned 503/connection reset over a 25-minute window. Average p95 latency outside the window remained within SLO.
- Fix applied: tweaked the autoscaler scale-in threshold and bump of initial pod buffer for FieldScale tenant at 2026-10-29T06:30:00 PDT. This eliminated immediate repro on our internal load test.
- Next steps: scheduled a controlled canary of the new autoscaler tuning for the tenant on Nov 1 during low traffic.

We recommend FieldScale apply a jittered exponential backoff (recommended max 3 retries with randomized delay 200–800ms) until we complete the canary.

Priyom
Priyom Das
On-call — Serving Runtime

Request from contract/procurement side: given the visible customer impact on Oct 28, we’d like Redwood to confirm whether this meets the partner SLA breach criteria and, if so, propose the mechanism for crediting or an exception. Our renewal conversation is active and procurement teams are watching.

Can you advise on how Redwood processes partner credit/exception requests? Also, will you share a short postmortem we can include in our internal update?

—Jordan

Jordan — thanks for confirming the retry behavior and for the timeline on your patch.

Summary and next steps from Redwood:
1) Root cause: transient autoscaler spin under a retry storm from older connector builds. We accept this as a platform-impacting event for the FieldScale tenant and will treat it as a partner SLA incident for the purposes of exception/credit review.
2) Immediate mitigations: we applied autoscaler tuning (Oct 29) and will run a controlled canary Nov 1; we recommend FieldScale patch connectors to use jittered exponential backoff (you said Nov 4 target).
3) Credits/exceptions: Procurement & Finance require: (a) a one-page postmortem, (b) quantified impacted token/request count, (c) your contractual tenant id and billing window. Once we have those we’ll route a formal credit recommendation through our Finance partner-team. I’ve attached a draft postmortem and the contract exception template for your convenience.
4) Action owners and deadlines:
   - FieldScale: send connector patch ETA and impacted customer list — Jordan — by COB Nov 4.
   - FieldScale: share exact tenant id(s) and billing windows for the affected requests — Jordan — by Nov 4.
   - Redwood: final postmortem + token impact calc — Camila (working with Priyom) — by Nov 5.
   - Redwood: finance recommendation submission — Laura Bennett — by Nov 9.

We’ll keep this thread updated. If you prefer a short sync (15–20m) to run through the postmortem and credit flow, I’m available Wednesday afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
